name: Lockheed T-33 Shooting Star
summary: Two-seat jet trainer derived from the P-80 Shooting Star that served in dozens of air forces; many ex-military 'T-Birds' are privately owned and fly as warbirds and adversary aircraft.

wings: Low, straight wing with large permanent tip tanks
engines: Single turbojet fed by flush side intakes ahead of the wing
fuselage: Long fuselage with a very long bubble canopy covering two tandem seats
tail: Tall single fin with a straight leading edge
Horizontal tail mounted mid-way on the fuselage

tellTales: Tip tanks on a straight wing and a very long canopy
Straight wings with a stretched fuselage and side intakes
Long, slim nose on a sleek early jet

confusedWith.howToTell: The Sabre has swept wings and a nose intake; the T-33 has straight wings, side intakes and tip tanks.
The L-29 has a pot-bellied fuselage with two separate canopies and no tip tanks; the T-33 has a long single canopy and big tip tanks.
The T-38 is a sleek twin-engine supersonic trainer with a pointed nose; the T-33 is a straight-wing single-engine jet.
The F-5 is a swept-wing twin-engine supersonic fighter; the T-33 is a straight-wing, tip-tank trainer.
